title: Ancient Wyvern
snippet:
Ancient Wyvern -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : The Ancient Wyvern presents a rather unique fight in that the player has the option to fight it by conventional means, or navigate the area to reach a location above it and perform a plunging attack that instantly slays the creature. Upon triggering the wyvern's entrance, the player should sprint underneath it and head left, reaching some ruins inhabited by several Man Serpents. It is important not to delay long in this area, as the boss will use its flame breath to incinerate anything inside. Once the player reaches a stone bridge, the fire cannot reach them, although a new threat presents itself in the form of a Giant Man Serpent with a retractable axe. It is strongly advised to lure this enemy back over the bridge before dashing past or engaging in combat.

title: Ancient Wyvern
snippet:
Upon reaching the wooden platforms behind the stone bridge, the wyvern will start breathing fire along the walkways. The player should take cover until the flames cease and immediately drop to the platform directly above the boss. From here, they can perform a plunging attack to instantly kill the monster; this is not without risk, however, as missing the hit will result in falling to their death. As the boss will stop moving and no longer attack the player once they are above it, a safer but longer method is to eliminate it with ranged weapons.

Alternatively, if the player does not wish to run the gauntlet, they can fight the wyvern in regular combat. It is recommended to stay under the boss to avoid its flame breath, although it will constantly attempt to crush them with its feet. Due to the wyvern's high vitality, it is recommended to attack its neck, head, and wings to inflict more damage.

title: Ancient Wyvern
snippet:
Ancient Wyvern -  Dark Souls III - boss - description 
 description : An imposing beast that will hinder the Ashen One's progress through Archdragon Peak. Typical of wyverns, it has two legs and two wings along with thick, ashen scales that are not easily penetrated. Its body features varying contours of green, red, and blue, which can perhaps be attributed to its age, speaking to the longevity of the wyvern. On its head it appears to have dense, horn-like scales, with its mouth complete with an elongated "mustache".

title: Ancient Wyvern
snippet:
Ancient Wyvern -  Dark Souls III - boss - notes 
 notes : It is possible to slay the Ancient Wyvern by executing a jumping attack from the bell platform behind it, when its head is near the player. Doing so requires good timing and that the wyvern is performing a specific attack. If executed properly, however, it can allow players to defeat the boss shortly after entering the arena.
After killing the Ancient Wyvern, the player will be teleported to the Dragon-kin Mausoleum bonfire. As the player has likely fallen down to the starting area of the arena after performing the plunging attack, this event saves the player the time that would otherwise be spent running through the entirety of the arena again.

title: Archdragon Peak
snippet:
Archdragon Peak -  Dark Souls III - location - lore 
 lore : Nowadays, Archdragon Peak is no longer inhabited by ancient dragons. However, their descendants, the Man Serpents, persisted and they serve as guards of the Peak. Darkeater Midir is also a descendant of the archdragons although he does not reside here but instead near the faraway Ringed City.

Those who desire to worship dragons often end up here, as evidenced by they many corpses of those who died trying. Those who choose the path of the dragons strive for perfect imitation, using the Dragon Head Stone at first, then the torso stone, imbued with the everlasting dragons' power. Special "twinkling" stones existed for the most fervent worshipers, who imbued them not only with a more advanced dragon-like form, but also a hovering mirage of an Archdragon. The way of worship and emulation was long and arduous and only those with the most fortitude could complete it.

title: Archdragon Peak
snippet:
Archdragon Peak can be entered only after learning the Path of the Dragon gesture found upon a corpse of a Drakeblood Knight in the Consumed King's Garden; this faction of knights can be summoned in Archdragon Peak by the man serpents there. Drakeblood Knights worshiped the blood of dragons; and the red cloth decorating their armor is said to symbolize their yearning for blood.

In Archdragon Peak, the Calamity Ring is found, reportedly made from the orange eye of a calamitous dragon, the ring considered a symbol of dragon worship. This dragon was none other than Black Dragon Kalameet, said to be the last one of ancient dragons.

The Nameless King, known for once allying with ancient dragons, resides on Archdragon Peak. He is accompanied by a stormdrake, which he tamed and fought alongside him. Dragon Slayer Ornstein's weapon and armor can be found laying around the Nameless King's arena; he was said to have left his guard in Anor Londo cathedral to search for the Nameless King.

title: Archdragon Peak
snippet:
Archdragon Peak -  Dark Souls III - location - trivia 
 trivia : This area draws heavily upon Byzantine architecture as inspiration for its appearance and design. The building that serves as the Dragon-Kin Mausoleum, in particular, bears a striking resemblance to churches (and mosques) designed in Byzantine tradition, the most famous icon of which is [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hagia_Sophia Hagia Sophia] in Istanbul, Turkey.
** Interestingly, it is possible that the architects of Hagia Sophia considered it the sacred ground of the *demiurge*—specifically, one that manifested through light and the sun. In the Neoplatonic school, the deific figure *demiurge* is the "fashioner" of the universal order, generally held to be distinct from "*the One*" which is the essential *form* of existence. These conceptions roughly parallel the Nameless King/Gwyn and the First Flame: the Chief Gods (the demiurge) sculpted the Age of Fire from Disparity (the One).

Anor Londo and Lothric can be seen on the horizon, far in the distance.
Most standard enemies here will not be able to detect a player hidden with the hidden body and Spook/slumbering dragoncrest ring combination. However, man serpent summoners can, as well as the mini boss and both main bosses.

title: Archdragon Peak
snippet:
Archdragon Peak -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : Archdragon Peak is an optional location that can be accessed by performing the "Path of the Dragon" gesture near the meditating dragon statue where the Dragon Torso Stone is found in the Irithyll Dungeon.

Archdragon Peak is populated by Man Serpents and Rock Lizards. It was seemingly built as a shrine to worship the Ancient Dragons by their descendants, the Man Serpents. Contrary to what its name implies, this area does not currently contain any true dragons, as those died long ago at the hands of the first Lords. The only dragons seemingly alive is the King of the Storm, the Nameless King's companion stormdrake mount, and the Ancient Wyverns. Archdragon Peak also overlooks on the body of an ancient dragon: the body can be seen clearly on the peak on the opposite side of the great bell.

The main boss of this area is The Nameless King.

title: Consumed King's Garden
snippet:
At the halfway point of the garden, Hawkwood's summon sign can be found, and to the right is an elevator leading to a shortcut. This elevator also has an intermediate floor that can be dropped down on, leading to the Dragonscale Ring and allowing you to kill the Lothric Priest that overlooks the knights in front of the door to Oceiros, the Consumed King.

Beyond Oceiros, there are chambers with dead Man Serpents, with one still alive. Here, two Titanite Scales can be looted from chests, the "Path of the Dragon" gesture can be obtained, and an illusory wall at the back hides the entrance to the Untended Graves.

title: Consumed King's Garden
snippet:
Consumed King's Garden -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : The Consumed King's Garden is accessible as soon as Dancer of the Boreal Valley is defeated. It is first accessed by an elevator guarded by a Consumed King's Knight. It consists of a lower swamp-like area where most of the ground is covered with Toxic-inflicting sludge, where Pus of Man roam, and a higher, stone-paved area where Consumed King's Knights stand guard.

The Garden is first accessed through an elevator guarded by a mace-wielding knight. You can drop down to an intermediate floor while going down to avoid having to traverse the toxic sludge and loot an Estus Shard and a Titanite Chunk.

A large stone platform is raised above the swamp where another mace-wielding knight stands guard, and below this are corpses carrying the Shadow Set, the Claws, three Black Firebombs and some Human Pine Resins. Some non-threatening Rotten Slugs also lurk here.

Consumed King's Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Consumed King's Knights fight identically to the Cathedral Knights, so similar tactics should be used against them. They wield either a greatsword or a mace with greatshield, and are very vulnerable to backstabs, although they will attempt guard breaks if this method is used against them. They have significantly more attack power and defense than their cathedral counterparts and can easily kill a player if they are cornered. Due to the toxicity of the garden, it is advised to fight them on dry land.

title: Dragon Eye
snippet:
Dragon Eye -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : Usage of the Dragon Eye is limited to players who are members of the Path of the Dragon covenant.

Using the Dragon Eye causes the player's sign to appear in the worlds of other players, allowing them to summon the user to their world to duel. The player does not need to be in human form. However, the host must be in human form (reverse-hollowed), but does not need to possess a Dragon Scale (contrary to the in-game description), and the area boss does not need to be alive to interact with the summon sign; users of the dragon eye have no such restrictions as to where and when they can place their signs. Players can summon others that are within their soul level +/-(10+10%) of their level; for example, a level 100 player can be summoned by anyone between level 80 and 120.

title: Dragon Head Stone
snippet: Unlike most other covenant-related items, the Dragon Head Stone does not require membership of its parent covenant to use. Leaving the Path of the Dragon covenant does not affect usage of the head stone in any way, though the player will lose any covenant rank-dependent benefits (the increased fire damage from the head stone, as well as the increased buff power and roar range of the Dragon Torso Stone).

title: Dragon Head Stone
snippet:
Dragon Head Stone -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Players must not be wearing headgear in order to use the Dragon Head Stone. In addition, they must not be suffering the egghead status effect. Once used, the player's head takes on the appearance of a dragon. The effect is permanent until the player's death.

Pressing and holding the [USE] button while the stone is in the current belt slot (X for Xbox 360, Square for PS3) emits fire breath at the cost of 50 stamina recovery per second squared. The direction the stream of fire travels in is perpendicular to the player's body, rather than the direction their head is actually facing. This means that unlike other ranged attacks, when using lock-on, the player must continue to move to update their direction in order to hit moving targets. The base damage the fire breath deals per tick increases along with the player's rank in the Path of the Dragon covenant—**120** at +0, **125** at +1, **130** at +2, and **140** at +3.

title: Dragon Torso Stone
snippet:
Dragon Torso Stone -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : When used, the Dragon Torso Stone transforms the player's body into that of a dragon-like creature. The transformation is permanent until the player dies, cannot be performed while wearing armor, and does *not* improve the player's defenses in any way. While transformed, the Stone can be re-activated at any time to cause the player to roar, at the cost of 100 stamina, with the following effects:
Emits a Force-like shockwave centered on the player, inflicting knockback to nearby enemies and reflecting projectiles. Its range, but not magnitude, will increase depending on the player's Path of the Dragon covenant rank—**2.5** meters at +0, **3** meters at +1, **3.5** meters at +2, and **4** meters at +3.

title: Drakeblood Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Drakeblood Knight (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - lore 
 lore : An order of knights who venerate dragon blood. The blade of their swords is engraved with script symbolizing dragon blood. Drakeblood Knights were worshippers of the blood of dragons and the red cloth that decorates their garments is said to symbolize their yearning for blood. In ages past they laid siege to a city in order to kill the slumbering dragon that slept there believing its blood would grant them true understanding of life. Led by Sir Yorgh they managed to kill the king of the city. However, when Yorgh attempted to kill the dragon with his spear, it awakened and spewed a cloud of toxic gas that enveloped the city, killing Sir Yorgh as well as most of the inhabitants and Drakeblood Knights.

It is said that dragon worship has captured the hearts and minds of warriors across the lands for many ages.

The summoner can call in Drakeblood Knights infinitely, although only one at a time. Once the summoner is dead, the last knight summoned will remain and he can then be killed permanently.

title: Drakeblood Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Drakeblood Knight (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Even when Drakeblood Knights don't have the same rolling penalty they had in *Dark Souls II*, they are much easier to defeat this time around. They boast a very high amount of health and can inflict both Magic and Lightning damage through shields, however, so they should not be underestimated.

They come armed with the Spirit Tree Crest Shield, which grants them high defense against lightning-based attacks, although they rarely use it and instead prefer to hold their greatswords with both hands. Their attacks are slow and amply telegraphed, and they usually don't chain more than three swings, which allow the player to counterattack without taking too much risk once they finish a combo.

They frequently attempt to use the Stance skill with their weapons, which the player can use to their advantage by luring them into swinging and missing in order to score some hits.

title: Drakeblood Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Drakeblood Knight (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - description 
 description : Drakeblood Knights make a return from their appearance in *Dark Souls II: Crown of the Sunken King*. They are clad in the Drakeblood Set and come armed with the Drakeblood Greatsword and the Spirit Tree Crest Shield. Their greatsword deals both Magic and Lightning damage, so they can still inflict some damage through shields. They boast a vast amount of vitality, but their combat tactics are quite predictable and easily avoided.

They appear exclusively as summons by the first Man Serpent Summoner in Archdragon Peak and their appearance in Lothric is not given much explanation other than they were worshippers of dragons and Archdragon Peak is a sanctuary known for those kind of cults.

title: Drakeblood Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Drakeblood Knight (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - enemy - farming 
 farming : Since Drakeblood Knights spawn infinitely and yield a base amount of 4,000 souls, they can be used for farming. By equipping the Symbol of Avarice, the Shield of Want, the Hornet Ring, the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring, and the Covetous Silver Serpent Ring (and perhaps also Aldrich's Ruby to alleviate some of the HP drain produced by the Symbol of Avarice), the player can maximize the amount of souls acquired for each knight killed.

The player just needs to stand behind their spawning spot and begin combat with a backstab, the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring will ensure they don't turn hostile prematurely and the Hornet Ring will increase the damage dealt, allowing the player to kill them with only a few more hits. Each knight defeated will yield 7,000+ souls and the process can be repeated as many times as necessary.

title: Drakeblood Knight (Dark Souls III)
snippet: Caution must be taken if the Man Serpent Summoner summons Havel, though, in which case it's best to make haste to the nearby bonfire and try again. If the true Havel has already been defeated, then the Summoner will only be able to summon Drakeblood Knights, allowing the farming process to continue without interruptions.

title: Giant Man Serpent
snippet:
Giant Man Serpent -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Giant Man Serpents are very dangerous enemies and should never be rushed; instead, they should be approached more strategically.

It is not recommended to confront them if there are other enemies around, so it's better to dispatch of all hostiles in the vicinity before even attempting to deal with them.

Once a Giant Man Serpent engages in battle, it will chase after the player relentlessly with surprising speed. Their long-reach weapons and excellent tracking may even allow them to successfully hit a player at medium distance whilst they are attempting to escape.

Fortunately, in all the locations where they are encountered, they can be lured near structures where it is possible to perform plunging attacks on them. Apart from receiving heavy damage, they will be left heavily staggered afterward and ready for a quick finish.

title: Giant Man Serpent
snippet:
Giant Man Serpent -  Dark Souls III - enemy - description 
 description : Towering above their lesser brethren, Giant Man Serpents comprise the elite forces of their race. They can be encountered either with groups of normal Man Serpents or even with others of their own, large-sized kind. They are surprisingly fast, almost equaling a sprinting player's speed, and will chase relentlessly for long distances once they engage in combat.

Their offensive capabilities are not restricted just to the weapons they wield; they have the ability to breathe devastating streams of fire, which they will spray in a clockwise arc in front of them.

If the player is attacking from behind, it may swing its neck around and grab them with its jaws, lifting them from the ground and lashing them back down for high damage.

There are two variants:

title: Item Discovery (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Item Discovery (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - overview 
 overview : Increasing Item Discovery improves the chance for enemies to drop items. It is useful for obtaining rare items that would be otherwise difficult to obtain.

It was originally a visible stat displayed on your character stats screen in *Dark Souls* that adjusted with factors like the items you wore and if you were human or hollow. In *Dark Souls II* the stat is hidden, but there are items that are known increase your item discovery. In addition, the Bonfire Intensity in the area also changes the Item Discovery of the area.

Every 100 Item discovery increases the odds of every possible item an enemy can drop to increase by 1%. Enemies in NG+ and Co-op may change the loot tables that are rolled when they die.

After meeting the beast at the gorge, who flys out of reach and breathes fire from up above, returning to Gough will have him ask about the encounter and if the dragon is causing the player trouble. snippet:

 how_to_join : The Mound-makers can be joined in the Undead Settlement. By navigating to a hidden area patrolled by numerous Thralls, the player can discover a non-hostile Hollow Manservant carrying an empty cage on its back. By examining the hollow, the player will enter the cage and be transported to the Pit of Hollows, below the Curse-rotted Greatwood's boss arena. This Manservant will be hostile if the Greatwood has been confronted or defeated, and thus cannot be interacted with.

Once there, the player must talk to Holy Knight Hodrick, who stands next to the covenant's Sacrificial Altar and who will give them the Mound-makers covenant item. If talked to again, he will give the player a Homeward Bone, which is required to leave the area without using the Darksign or committing suicide.

The Fire Keeper in Firelink Shrine will react with a corresponding gesture of her own if the player performs one in front of her. Depending on the gesture selected, she will respond with either a bow, a laugh, a twirl, or even by turning her head away in disapproval.
** Performing the "Path of the Dragon" gesture in front of her will cause her to continually twirl.
The "Stretch Out" gesture can allow the player to evade certain horizontal attacks. A notable example is the Demon Prince's laser attack.
A Hollow is used as the avatar for the gesture options.

title: Gestures (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Gestures (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - description 
 description : Gestures are special animations the player can perform, often used as a means of communicating with other players. Among other things, gestures can be used to greet another player, thank them or making them aware of a nearby treasure.

The player starts the game with several gestures already at their disposal. These can be consulted and managed by pressing the button, bringing up a list with seven gestures ready for use. To perform a gesture, select it and press the action button ( / ) or / .

As more gestures are learned, the player can press / to open a complete menu of all the player's collected gestures. From here, gestures can either be added to the quick menu by selecting them or used directly by pressing / .

Additional gestures can be learned throughout the course of the game. These are usually learned from other characters, after performing certain actions, or after defeating certain enemies.

title: Man Serpent (Lore)
snippet: The current king of Lothric, Oceiros, also showed great interest in dragons, and seems to have taken hold of some of the Man Serpents, which now reside in the deepest parts of his personal garden. Perhaps he sought to discover something about dragons from their descendants, or he was merely looking for the location of the Archdragon Peak.

Killing the Sulyvahn's beasts is not required to join the covenant. If one wears the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring and casts Hidden Body just as they reach the bottom of the ladder, they can sneak around the left, far wall and avoid the beasts and pray to McDonnell, thus joining.

title: Gestures (Dark Souls II)
snippet:

 lead : **Gestures** are player actions in *Dark Souls II*. A few are received at the start of the game, and more are taught by certain NPCs throughout the game. Usually to learn the gesture one has to exhaust all dialogue with the NPC.

Unlike the first *Dark Souls*, players can cancel out of a gesture's animation by rolling or backstepping.

Learning all 20 gestures unlocks the Achievement/Trophy "Gesture Maestro", worth 50 Gamerscore or a Silver Trophy respectively.

title: Gestures
snippet:

title: Rat King (covenant)
snippet:
Rat King (covenant) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Talk to the Rat King, located in either the Grave of Saints or the Doors of Pharros, after their respective bosses. While a Rat Tail is required to join the king's covenant, it's unlikely that players won't have one when they meet him, especially since they are dropped by the bosses who need to be defeated in order to reach him in the first place. Upon accepting his offer, players will be awarded the Crest of the Rat.

title: Undead Match
snippet:
These online battles are similar to those found in previous games, with the exception that there are no special arenas designed specifically for them this time around, and instead they take place in normal locations visited during the main game, such as the Kiln of the First Flame and Archdragon Peak.

Winning multiple times will reward the player with an insignia next to their name which represents the amount of victories they have accumulated on that character. There are two insignias, one for free-for-all and one for team fights. No items or souls are awarded during or after an Undead Match. Similarly, souls won't be lost nor will hollowing increase if the player dies within an Undead Match, although consumed items will not be restored, and broken equipment will not be repaired.

title: Gestures
snippet:
Gestures -  Dark Souls - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : For practical purposes, gestures can be used by players to indicate to one another the right direction or action to take when at a junction. Gestures are more commonly used to indicate emotions, as well as for taunting.

Gestures require time to perform. During this time, the player is as vulnerable to attacks as if they were standing still. Gestures can only be cancelled by initiating another gesture, or being attacked. Therefore, it's best to perform gestures out of harm's way. (As of Dark Souls 3, gestures can be cancelled by performing any action or pressing any button and do not have to be completed).

title: Homeward (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Use of Homeward and other bonfire-warping items reset the area and all respawnable enemies, but it does not reset the character nor does it count as resting. Unlike other warping-items, Homeward isn't useful for no bonfire runs since it requires attunement, which requires resting. Even in NG+, the Aged Feather is better suited. Note that Estus Flasks and spell casts will not recharge as a result.

This spell, along with the Darksign, Aged Feather, and Homeward Bones will warp you back to the spawn gazebo in Things Betwixt if both the Fire Keeper's Dwelling in Things Betwixt and The Far Fire in Majula are unlit, potentially as a softlock prevention measure and/or a default warp location.

This is the only spell that will always have one cast, no matter what Attunement level the player is at. However, the use of items that grant extra casts, such as the Saint's Hood or a Northern Ritual Band variant, can be used to increase the number of spell casts.

title: Caestus
snippet:
Caestus -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The caestus deals very low damage and has a short reach, in exchange for a relatively fast attack speed.
Although it deals less damage than the Claw, it can be obtained much earlier.
Due to its size, wearing concealing clothing or using certain effects can 'mask' the fact the player is wielding the Caestus. With a Ring of Fog in PvP, the player would look like they are bare-handed and friendly until they get a backstab or riposte. In PvE, the Caestus does deal enough damage to give the player a chance of survival against weak or humanoid enemies like Hollows, but against tougher enemies a better weapon would be required.
